items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: No. One time you know he stopped a take and I got pissed. But I got along with the guys you know.

ctx.x: Did you ever butt heads with Bernard Purdie?

No. One time you know he stopped a take and I got pissed. But I got along with the guys you know. First of all I was a child producer I’m telling you. I started producing when I was like 20. So all these guys were older than me. And it was kind of, I kind of grew up in the studio with them you know? Like King Curtis was a great friend and he helped me a lot, he hipped me to a lot of stuff. I mean I always describe myself in those days as having one foot in hip and the other foot in huh, because I really didn’t…
Did the amount of records that sold make a difference in your income?
